meta.rate_basis: Implied by IFRC Emergency Appeal MDRNP022 (Aug 2026): NPR 500,000 ~ CHF 2,700 (185) and NPR 90,000 ~ CHF 480 (187.5); 185 used. Not a market quote.
meta.usd_basis: WFP 2024 Koshi anticipatory activation: NPR 15,000 = USD 113.3 (132.4), rounded to 133; USD-to-CHF is derived via NPR, not market rate.
meta.estimate_flag: Items with estimate=true are derived or assumed (see cost_basis). unit_cost null means no Nepal source found; not guessed.

actions.name: Upstream detection to direct alarm chain (multi-sensor trigger -> cell broadcast, sirens, hydropower control rooms, police)
actions.implementer: DHM (detection, alarm), NDRRMA (cell broadcast, order), Nepal Telecom/Ncell, operators (receive); China hydromet/Kyirong authorities (cross-border feed)
actions.cost_basis: Cell-broadcast set-up USD 1.75-3 M (GSMA/ITU estimate quoted by Mongabay) converted at NPR 133/USD; sensors/seismic/camera upstream NOT costed (no source found).
actions.people_per_unit: whole corridor population (679,295 SMS recipients in 4 districts on 26 Aug 2026)
actions.evidence: 2026 event: first public alert 38 min after collapse (23 min to DHM via District Administration phone call, 15 min to dispatch); upstream gauges were lost 13 min after collapse; flood reached Syabrubesi ~10 min after border crossing; Nepal-China data sharing mechanism agreed 2025 but not operational. No evaluation of detection-to-alarm chains for ice-rock avalanches in Nepal.
actions.risks: False alarms from non-hazard seismic signals (DMG classified the 4.4 signal as non-earthquake and issued no alert); sensors destroyed by the event itself; cross-border politics; alarm without a pre-agreed receiver protocol is useless (see EA02, EA09).

actions.name: Hydropower underground works (tunnel/adit/powerhouse/cavern) alarm-triggered evacuation protocol and muster points
actions.implementer: Project operators and contractors (Upper Trishuli-1/3A/3B, Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, Langtang Khola), NEA, IPPAN; labour inspectors
actions.unit: per project (alarm receiver, siren/PA, signed-off drill, count-in/count-out system)
actions.cost_basis: No Nepal cost data found; cost is dominated by drills and paid worker time, not hardware. Not estimated.
actions.people_per_unit: 40-600 underground/camp workers per project (UT-1: 573 unaccounted; UT-3B: 122; Rasuwagadhi: 93; Trishuli 3A: 40-45 present vs normal 5-6)
actions.evidence: 2026: ~800-934 hydropower-linked people unaccounted for (IPPAN/energy minister, 23 Sep >800); two Trishuli-3A staff survived 9 days underground; an ADB expert panel had recommended upstream/downstream alert coordination and evacuation protocols, apparently not in place; no report of any operator alarm. No peer-reviewed evidence on tunnel evacuation in debris floods.
actions.risks: Mobile phones do not work underground (a worker warned his family of this); tunnel entrances buried (adit exits are the flood path); shift-count uncertainty; evacuation upslope may be through the same portal that floods; production-loss pressure causes alarm fatigue.

actions.name: Headworks / intake gate, sluice and powerhouse isolation sequence on external alarm
actions.implementer: Plant operators, NEA grid control
actions.unit: per hydropower plant (automatic logic + manual override)
actions.cost_basis: Not costed; engineering study needed. Likely retrofit of existing SCADA.
actions.people_per_unit: plant-level (asset protection; benefit to people indirect via downstream surge attenuation, which is unproven for debris flows)
actions.evidence: No evidence found that gate operation attenuates a debris flood of this magnitude; 12-15 plants (431 MW) were damaged. Treat as hypothesis. Jure 2014 landslide dam damaged Sunkoshi and Bhotekoshi plants (headworks destroyed).
actions.risks: Closing intake gates can raise upstream water level; automatic trips may destabilise national grid; cannot protect underground works unless the alarm also evacuates people (EA02).

actions.name: Cell-broadcast alert with action-specific, multilingual text (Nepali, Tamang, English, Chinese) for corridor cells
actions.implementer: NDRRMA (lead agency named), Nepal Telecom, Ncell, DHM
actions.cost_basis: USD 1.75-3 M set-up (GSMA/ITU as quoted in Mongabay; not independently verified) at NPR 133/USD.
actions.people_per_unit: all handsets in targeted cells (~10 s delivery claimed)
actions.evidence: 26 Aug 2026 SMS used the routine monsoon template, Nepali only, no location/time/shelter info; one SMS received 19 min late; generic repeated alerts have eroded trust (scoping review of 38 studies cited by Mongabay). Cell broadcast not procured at time of event. Peer-reviewed evidence on cell broadcast for flash floods exists outside Nepal but was not reviewed here.
actions.risks: Alert fatigue; handsets off or no signal in gorges; towers destroyed (communications were down in Rasuwa/Nuwakot/Dhading); legal gap: DHM may warn but not order evacuation.

actions.name: Mass SMS/IVR with distinct "extreme event - move now" template, voice IVR for low literacy
actions.implementer: DHM, NDRRMA, Nepal Telecom, Ncell
actions.cost_basis: ASSUMPTION: bulk SMS tariff NPR 0.1-0.5; no Nepal tariff verified. 679,295 messages sent 26 Aug 2026 -> NPR 68k-340k per full blast (estimate).
actions.people_per_unit: 1 per message (679,295 recipients on 26 Aug 2026)
actions.evidence: See EA04; Nepal Red Cross sEAP 2025 developed SMS/IVR, radio jingle and social media messages and disseminated via FM, SMS, siren systems (not activated in 2025).
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
actions.risks: Template reuse trains people to ignore alerts; delivery delay under congestion (SMS is not 10 s); language.

actions.name: Community siren / loudspeaker / runner network at riverside settlements (CBFEWS node)
actions.implementer: Palikas/ward offices, community disaster management committees, NRCS sub-chapters, Practical Action-style CBFEWS
actions.unit: per community early-warning system (gauge + siren + comms)
actions.cost_basis: Himalayan Times opinion piece (undated, secondary): purchase NPR 400,000 + install NPR 500,000 + O&M NPR 130,000/yr; first-year total NPR 1.03 M. Not verified against a primary source.
actions.people_per_unit: hundreds to thousands per community (Karnali CBFEWS reaches ~52,000 Nepalis per a thesis abstract)
actions.evidence: Rai et al. 2020 (IJDRR): CBA of Karnali flood EWS - reported BCR 24-73 and avoided loss NPR 117,027/household (figures read from a search-engine summary; abstract page not accessed); +1 h lead time raises savings 1.83x; Smith et al. 2017: DHM forecasting raised Karnali lead time from 2-3 h to 7-8 h. Applies to slow monsoon floods, not minutes-scale debris floods; Imja Tsho GLOF siren network reported rusting (April 2026 BBC-sourced reports).
actions.risks: Maintenance decay (Imja); gauges designed for gradual rise miss high-velocity floods (4 stations destroyed 26 Aug); sirens need a person who decides; false alarms.

actions.name: School alert-to-assembly protocol and evacuation drills (move to pre-mapped high ground; head-count; students in transit)
actions.implementer: Schools (head teachers), palika education units, Ministry of Education, NRCS junior/youth circles
actions.unit: per school (SOP, route marking, annual drill)
actions.cost_basis: Not costed in sources; low unit cost (staff time). sEAP example: 11 community SIMEX with 636 participants funded within CHF 11,510 shelter readiness line (not separable).
actions.people_per_unit: ~900 students on campus at Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School, Bidur (school roll 1,643-1,650; sources differ)
actions.evidence: 26 Aug 2026: head teacher ordered ~900 students to higher ground ~9:10 after phone calls; flood hit ~10 min later and buried the compound; students en route to school were unaccounted for. Single anecdote, not an evaluation.
actions.risks: Children in transit and at home; warning arrived informally (friends/relatives) before official SMS; false alarm cost = lost class time; reliance on a single decision-maker.

actions.name: Pre-mapped evacuation routes and elevated safe points with signage, vertical evacuation where terrain permits
actions.implementer: Palikas, DDMC/LDMC, NRCS
actions.cost_basis: sEAP: 17 evacuation centres mapped across Kailali/Banke/Bardiya (capacity ~1,000 people); mapping done in a single July 2024 exercise; unit cost not given.
actions.people_per_unit: ~60 per centre in sEAP example (1,000/17); riverside settlements in gorges need far larger capacity
actions.evidence: Used in sEAP drills; relatives of one 2026 survivor reached high ground but were still caught by waves, i.e. route length vs. 10-min travel time matters.
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
actions.risks: Slope instability on routes; mapping done for water floods, not debris-flow runout; elderly/PwD cannot move fast.

actions.name: Highway and border-crossing hold: close Pasang Lhamu Highway / Rasuwagadhi crossing and Prithvi/Mugling-Narayanghat corridors on trigger
actions.implementer: Nepal Police, APF, Department of Roads, customs (Rasuwagadhi), district administration; Chinese border authorities
actions.cost_basis: Not costed; main cost is economic (stopped trade/traffic) and liability for wrongful closure.
actions.people_per_unit: dozens to hundreds of vehicles/pedestrians per hour at the border; traders, pilgrims, drivers
actions.evidence: 26 Aug 2026: closure advisories for Prithvi Highway, Galchhi-Nuwakot-Rasuwa-Syabrubesi road, Mugling-Narayangadh went out ~10:28 and ~11:50 (downstream), i.e. after the flood reached the border; Rasuwagadhi crossing, Kyirong road destroyed. Foreigners among missing include pilgrims, traders and drivers at the crossing.
actions.risks: Time to the border is ~minutes after trigger: only useful for downstream segments; closures at false alarms cost trade and trust.

actions.name: Trekker/lodge alert (registered mobile numbers from TIMS/permits, lodge radio tree) for Langtang and Rasuwa corridors
actions.implementer: Nepal Tourism Board, TAAN/NMA, Langtang National Park, lodge associations, palikas
actions.cost_basis: Not costed; integration with cell broadcast (EA04) makes marginal cost near zero. Estimate absent.
actions.people_per_unit: hundreds of trekkers per day in peak season (Aug is monsoon low season)
actions.evidence: 26 Aug 2026: 403 tourists untraceable (341 foreign, 62 Nepali, per Nepalnews); debris bypassed main Langtang trekking valley but trekkers were still listed missing; SMS was Nepali only.
actions.risks: Foreign SIMs not on Nepali networks; unregistered trekkers; language.

actions.name: Door-to-door volunteer warning and early evacuation of riverside households to pre-identified centres
actions.implementer: NRCS volunteers and sub-chapters, palika ward offices, early warning task forces
actions.cost_basis: NRCS sEAP trigger 26-28 Sep 2024: ~CHF 600 spent, 3,600 people received warnings (102 volunteers) -> ~CHF 0.17/person (~NPR 31 at 185). Marginal activation cost only; readiness/pre-positioning adds CHF ~36.7 per targeted person (CHF 199,964 / 5,454 people over 2 years).
actions.people_per_unit: ~35 people per volunteer (3,600/102)
actions.evidence: First Nepal Red Cross EAP: activated once (Sept 2024, de-escalated after 48 h, little rain in target area; heavy rain fell in Kathmandu valley outside the target area); never triggered in 2025. Process evidence only, no impact evaluation. 3-day forecast with staged alerts (72 h) rehearsed in 11 SIMEX in 2025.
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 Operations Update 30 Oct 2024)
https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
actions.risks: False alarm / wrong location (Sept 2024); volunteer attrition (110 -> 99); trigger statements inconsistent with DHM bulletins; works for river floods with hours of lead time, not for 10-minute debris floods.

actions.name: Livestock and household-asset evacuation (pre-agreed transport providers, shelters)
actions.implementer: NRCS district chapters, palikas, transport providers, livestock service offices
actions.cost_basis: sEAP: standing agreements with local transport providers renewed 2025; no unit price in reports.
actions.people_per_unit: per household; Pople et al.: cash recipients were 17 pp more likely to evacuate livestock (Bangladesh)
actions.evidence: Pople et al. 2026 (WBER) and Gros et al. 2019/2023 on anticipatory cash (Bangladesh): recipients evacuated assets/livestock more; ECMWF workshop slide lists ~4-5 days lead for livestock moves in Brahmaputra context.
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
actions.risks: Needs >=6-24 h; not usable for minutes-scale events.

actions.name: Protect documents and essential assets: waterproof bags, shelter toolkits
actions.implementer: NRCS, FAO (hermetic grain bags), palikas
actions.cost_basis: sEAP pre-positioned 2,000 waterproof bags + 80 shelter toolkit sets (2024); unit prices not published in the reports read. OCHA 2025: FAO hermetic bags for 7,000 households (FAO sector budget USD 405,400 incl. co-funding).
actions.people_per_unit: 1 bag per household (~4-5 people; household size is an assumption)
actions.evidence: No effectiveness evaluation found.
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
https://www.unocha.org/ (OCHA Nepal CERF AA framework 2025, local copy: aa_nepal25.pdf)
actions.risks: People carry bags only if they have time; low marginal life-safety value.

actions.name: Pre-position and stage search-and-rescue (Army, APF, Police, NRCS) incl. tunnel-rescue kit (air pumping, excavators, drones, helicopters)
actions.implementer: Nepal Army, APF, Nepal Police, NDRRMA, NRCS, hydropower companies
actions.cost_basis: Not costed. 26 Aug 2026: Army prioritised 19 hydropower tunnels; access (bridges/roads washed away, entrances buried) was the main obstacle; survivors reached after 9 days.
actions.people_per_unit: hundreds trapped (639 trapped at UT-1 and 3A at one count; >100 maybe in tunnels at 29 Aug)
actions.evidence: 2026 event: 13,396 rescued by 7 Sep; 254 rescued from UT-1 by Army by 29 Aug. Counterfactual benefit of pre-staging not measured.
actions.risks: Staging at false alarms; corridors cut by event, so staging must be on the correct side of bridges.

actions.name: Pre-position medical supplies, ambulances, blood and trauma teams at downstream hubs
actions.implementer: Ministry of Health, hospitals (Bidur, Trishuli, Dhunche), NRCS (ambulance, blood bank, Red Cross Emergency Clinic)
actions.cost_basis: Not costed. IFRC appeal 2026 mentions NRCS Red Cross Emergency Clinic deployment and coverage of blood fees.
actions.people_per_unit: n/a
actions.evidence: No Nepal evaluation; standard humanitarian practice.
actions.risks: Event mortality in debris floods is mostly drowning/burial: few survivors needing trauma care (majority missing, not injured).

actions.name: Anticipatory multipurpose cash (SRSP standard NPR 5,000 or 8,000 by household size) via Local Disaster Management Fund bank transfer + SMS
actions.implementer: Palikas (LDMC/LDMF) with UNICEF, WFP, FAO; NRCS/IFRC
actions.cost_basis: OCHA/CERF Nepal AA framework 2025: transfer NPR 5,000 or 8,000 per household by household size (Shock-Responsive Social Protection and Relief Distribution Standard); other Nepal values: WFP 2022 USD 117; WFP 2024 Koshi NPR 15,000 (USD 113.3); IFRC 2026 post-event livelihoods grant NPR 90,000 (CHF 480; conditional, not anticipatory).
actions.people_per_unit: ~4-5 per household (assumption; Nepal census mean not re-verified)
actions.evidence: WFP/DIME RCT Nepal 2022 (3 days before flood): FCS +6%, 19% fewer rely on less preferred food, 25% fewer borrow food, anxiety/depression -3%; benefits faded once control group was paid; 50% of recipients got cash within 6 days of peak. Christian et al. 2025 RCT Bangladesh+Nepal: timely cash raises food security and psychosocial well-being (NBER abstract only; effect sizes not read). Pople et al. 2026: Bangladesh cash 5 days ahead -> improved welfare for 3 months, less asset loss, evacuations +12 pp. Gros 2019/2023: Bangladesh quasi-experimental.
source_urls: https://www.unocha.org/ (OCHA Nepal CERF AA framework 2025, local copy: aa_nepal25.pdf)
actions.risks: Needs river-flood lead time >=1-3 days; targeting (community nomination lacks precision); bank-account coverage; not applicable to minute-scale cascades; trade-off speed vs precision (WFP).

actions.name: Hygiene/dignity kits, water purification tablets/bleaching powder, buckets, emergency toilets pre-positioned and delivered to evacuation centres
actions.implementer: NRCS, UNICEF, UNFPA, palikas
actions.cost_basis: sEAP: 1,100 dignified hygiene kits procured via IFRC (contents listed; price not published); WASH readiness CHF 1,834 + pre-position CHF 22,293 (budget lines).
actions.people_per_unit: 1 kit/household; 60 volunteers trained in water purification
actions.evidence: Process documentation only; kits not used in 2024/25 triggers (no evacuation). UNICEF CERF AA WASH budget USD 171,100.
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
https://www.unocha.org/ (OCHA Nepal CERF AA framework 2025, local copy: aa_nepal25.pdf)
actions.risks: Stock rotation/expiry; little value if no one reaches centres.

actions.name: Activate evacuation centres with tarpaulins, blankets, mattresses, shelter toolkits
actions.implementer: NRCS, palikas, IFRC
actions.cost_basis: sEAP pre-positioned 800 tarpaulins, 800 blankets, 800 mattresses (2025); shelter pre-position budget CHF 27,643; unit prices not given.
actions.people_per_unit: 800 sets for 22 communities
actions.evidence: Not activated; for post-event displacement: IFRC 2026: 6,000+ homes completely damaged, people in open spaces and neighbours' homes.
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
actions.risks: Mountain access; cold at altitude (warm clothing).

actions.name: Hydropower and construction-site stand-down on forecast extreme rain (move equipment/camps out of floodplain, pause river-bed works, stop tunnel shifts)
actions.implementer: Operators, contractors, NEA, labour/safety inspectors, IPPAN
actions.cost_basis: Not costed: cost = lost production/construction time; to be estimated with operators.
actions.people_per_unit: 40-600 workers/project
actions.evidence: Spotlight Nepal: DHM 8:00 bulletin on 26 Aug flagged high flash flood risk in several districts but no standing protocol required action; applies to rainfall floods (Melamchi 2021, Sept 2024) not to the ice-rock avalanche which no forecast could target.
actions.risks: Routine bulletins are over-triggered: needs impact-based threshold to avoid constant stoppage.

actions.name: Landslide-dam lake response: daily monitoring, downstream evacuation, controlled breach/spillway, operator notification
actions.implementer: DHM, Dept of Mines & Geology, NDRRMA, Army, palikas, operators
actions.cost_basis: Not costed.
actions.people_per_unit: all downstream settlements and plants within reach
actions.evidence: Jure 2014: Sunkoshi dammed (55 m dam), flow stopped ~12 h at a gauge 38 km downstream (3 h after slide); several hydropower plants hit. 2026: DHM said the upstream dammed site "had not fully cleared" 5 h after crossing; secondary-flood risk flagged by IFRC. Melamchi 2021: local authorities warned after detecting the dam, 17-21 deaths incl. foreign workers (death tolls vary by source).
actions.risks: Poor access to monitor; unpredictable breach time; evacuation fatigue over weeks.

actions.name: Glacier/lake precursor watch and seasonal exclusion zones (cameras, InSAR/optical lake mapping, no-camp rules in runout zones)
actions.implementer: DHM, ICIMOD, DMG, universities, operators, palikas
actions.cost_basis: Not costed. Imja Tsho precedent: USD 3.5 M project incl. lake lowering (3.5 m) and EWS (search summary; not primary).
actions.people_per_unit: all downstream exposure
actions.evidence: Area was a "blind spot" for Nepal/China/international geologists; ICIMOD: only 7 of 38 monitored glaciers met a global benchmark; satellites cannot show fracture development; a report issued about a year before the July 2025 Rasuwagadhi flood had called for cross-border EWS, risk assessment and relocation of high-risk settlements (unimplemented, per press).
actions.risks: Slope failures often have no detectable precursor; many false positives.

actions.name: Seasonal readiness package: hazard/runout mapping, evacuation-centre mapping, SIMEX drills, early-warning task forces, standby transport, volunteer protocol, EW message pre-agreement
actions.implementer: NRCS, palikas, DHM, NDRRMA, DDMC
actions.cost_basis: sEAP2024NP01 total CHF 199,964 (readiness 71,592; pre-positioning 57,252; early action 71,038) for 22 communities -> CHF ~9,090 per community (NPR ~1.68 M) over 2 years; targeted 5,454 people -> CHF ~36.7 per person. Derived by me.
actions.people_per_unit: ~250 people per community (5,454 targeted/22)
actions.evidence: Process evidence: 11 SIMEX (636 participants), 17 evacuation centres, 99-110 trained volunteers; early-warning task forces newly formed in 2025 (none existed before). No outcome evaluation (never fully activated).
source_urls: https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 2025 Annual Report, Nepal flood)
https://go-api.ifrc.org/api/DownloadFile/ (IFRC GO: sEAP2024NP01 Operations Update 30 Oct 2024)
actions.risks: Volunteer attrition; protocols not refreshed; trigger statement inconsistent with DHM bulletins; calibrated for monsoon river floods not cryosphere cascades.

actions.name: Bilateral China-Nepal real-time data sharing and joint warning SOP for Rasuwagadhi/Kyirong (gauges, cameras, seismic)
actions.implementer: Ministries of Foreign Affairs/Energy/Home, DHM, China Ministry of Water Resources & Tibet hydromet
actions.cost_basis: Not costed.
actions.people_per_unit: whole downstream corridor (potential lead time gain: flood reached the border ~8:40; DHM informed ~8:56-9:00)
actions.evidence: Nepal and China agreed to set up a bilateral water-hazard data-sharing mechanism after the 2025 flood; not operational on 26 Aug 2026; "China's side was equally unaware". Current practice routes information via Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
actions.risks: Political; data sensitivity; Chinese-side sensors also vulnerable.

actions.name: Legal/SOP: DHM extreme-event warning triggers pre-authorised evacuation orders by LDMC/DDMC and operators (no-regret list)
actions.implementer: NDRRMA, Ministry of Home Affairs, DHM, palikas
actions.cost_basis: Not costed.
actions.people_per_unit: n/a
actions.evidence: Mongabay: DHM can warn but not order evacuation; no law triggers evacuation automatically; 2022 study of the 2021 rainfall disaster (120 deaths) recommended binding SOPs, not implemented. Spotlight: DHM budget fell NPR 765 M -> 338 M (-56%) between FY 2078/79 and 2081/82.
actions.risks: Over-triggering without calibrated thresholds; liability.

actions.name: Community-based forecast tool and lead-time extension (probabilistic forecast for DHM, 2-3 h -> 7-8 h) for rainfall flash floods
actions.implementer: DHM, Practical Action, universities
actions.cost_basis: Not costed in the abstract.
actions.people_per_unit: Karnali basin communities
actions.evidence: Smith et al. 2017 NHESS: Karnali lead time raised from 2-3 h to 7-8 h; last-mile communication of probabilistic forecasts remains the challenge. Rai et al. 2020: each additional hour multiplies savings (reported 1.83x).
actions.risks: Does not apply to ice-rock avalanche sources; gauges destroyed by large floods.
